statement: The first line holds n and m - nodes 0 to n-1 and undirected edges. The next m lines each hold an edge as two node numbers. Print yes when the graph contains a cycle and no otherwise. Walk every component, remembering for each discovered node who discovered it. Meeting an already-visited neighbour is a cycle - unless that neighbour is the node's own parent, since every undirected edge is seen once from each side. The graph may be disconnected: the outer loop over all nodes is part of the answer.

example.why: The four edges close a square; the walk meets a visited node that is nobody's parent.

hint: Carry the parent through the queue or the recursion; exempt exactly that one neighbour.
mistake: Reporting the reverse copy of the discovery edge as a cycle - every tree then looks cyclic.
